notes: §1985:VI.6.11.4 GR6 defines the remainder as 'the result of subtracting the product of the quotient (identifier-3) and the divisor from the dividend' and the quotient used, for a numeric edited or ROUNDED identifier-3, as an intermediate field with 'the same number of digits, the same decimal point location, and the same presence or absence of a sign as the quotient (identifier-3)'. ArithmeticEmitter.EmitDivideRemainder implements the truncated, unedited quotient at identifier-3's scale (SubsidiaryShapeOf; NativeSubsidiaryQuotient divides in the Int128 kernel under TRUNCATION, CarriedSubsidiaryQuotient/FixedPointSubsidiary truncate the final-transfer quotient) and forms dividend - subsidiary x divisor: correct at 85 for a signed identifier-3 and for any non-negative quotient, which is all the witness (11 / 3 GIVING PIC 9 ROUNDED, quotient 4, remainder 2) exercises. PARTIAL: the member has no edition arm, so the subsidiary quotient is always SIGNED, the 2023 rule (§2023:14.9.12.4 GR6 'a subsidiary quotient is developed that is signed'); at --std 85 an UNSIGNED identifier-3 (numeric PIC 9 or an edited item with no sign symbol, with or without ROUNDED) receiving a negative quotient stores its absolute value yet the remainder is computed from the negative quotient. DIVIDE -11 BY 3 GIVING QU (PIC 9) REMAINDER RM (PIC S99) stores QU = 3 and RM = -02 where the 1985 rule gives -11 - (3 x 3) = -20. No kb/Work note owns the fix (grepped 'presence or absence of a sign', VI.6.11.4, REMAINDER in PB5069-PB5130): the orchestrator files one.

next.reason: 1985: "the same presence or absence of a sign as the quotient (identifier-3)"; 2023: "a subsidiary quotient is developed that is signed and derived from the quotient by truncation of digits". Both define remainder as dividend minus truncated quotient times divisor, but 2023 always uses a signed subsidiary quotient. 1985 follows identifier-3's sign, so unsigned quotients differ.
